## Answer

This is a 2-step Carnot group: horizontal part $V\times V\cong\mathbb R^{12}$, center $Z=\bigwedge^2V/\mathbb R\omega\cong\mathbb R^{14}$, with bracket $[(v_1,v_2),(w_1,w_2)]=\overline{v_1\wedge w_1+v_2\wedge w_2}$. The bracket is surjective onto $Z$.

For 2-step Carnot groups, the Riemannian filling area of a horizontal loop of length $n$ is governed by the central (signed-area) component, which scales like $n^2$. This gives the quadratic upper bound, and the quadratic lower bound comes from loops enclosing large central area. So $a=2$.

The logarithmic factor is the step I did not derive. I am relying on recollection of the literature on sharp Dehn functions of 2-step nilpotent groups, where a single $\log$ correction to the quadratic bound appears for certain bracket structures. I believe this group falls in that class, giving $b=1$, but I have not verified this by computation, so treat the exponent of the logarithm as the least certain part.

ANSWER: (2, 1)
